source_snapshot.procedure: Verify the SUT recipe, clear logs, run `nvidia-smi -pm 1`, `dcgmi diag -v -r memtest`, then `nvidia-smi -pm 0`; collect results/photos and unexpected logs.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek substitutes undocumented `dcgmi diag --memtest`, calls the diagnostic read-only, omits the source persistence-mode transitions and provides no explicit GPU target.

original_test_intent.purpose: Exercise GPU memory with the DCGM memtest patterns on every in-scope NVIDIA GPU and verify the named diagnostic completes with PASS and no unexplained memory, GPU, driver or platform errors.
original_test_intent.target: All NVIDIA GPUs required by the selected SUT recipe. Because the source command supplies no entity selector, current DCGM defaults to all GPUs/all NVIDIA CPUs; the memtest result must account for every expected GPU rather than silently testing a subset.
original_test_intent.scope: One verbose named `memtest` diagnostic with the installed supported DCGM plugin/configuration, including its built-in software checks, while the approved GPUs are workload-free. Preserve and restore each GPU's original persistence-mode state instead of blindly leaving all GPUs disabled.
original_test_intent.operation: Inventory GPUs and clients, record per-GPU persistence/MIG/ECC/health/thermal state and logs, confirm compatible DCGM support and owner authorization, enable persistence only where required, run the documented named memtest with explicit auditable target coverage, collect complete diagnostic/telemetry evidence, then restore each original persistence state and verify final health.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: One iteration. The source provides a 40-minute machine-time estimate but no command timeout or exact required runtime; the diagnostic's actual pattern duration is GPU/configuration dependent and must not be replaced by a shorter arbitrary run.
original_test_intent.expected_result: Every expected GPU receives a completed memtest result of PASS, no requested test is skipped or unavailable, no unexplained ECC/XID/thermal/driver/platform event occurs, and all per-GPU persistence and service state returns to the recorded baseline.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: DCGM/driver/plugin versions, expected-to-observed GPU UUID/entity map, MIG/client inventory, per-GPU persistence baseline, exact command/config/hash, complete verbose or JSON output with per-entity status/timing, synchronized ECC/XID/thermal/driver/OS/BMC evidence, exit status and per-GPU restoration proof.
ambiguities: The source does not identify the qualified DCGM/driver version, plugin/configuration, GPU entity map, timeout or coverage parameters.
The 40-minute machine-time estimate is not an explicit acceptance duration and official pattern runtimes vary by GPU/configuration.
Unconditional `nvidia-smi -pm 0` can change a GPU that was already persistence-enabled before the test.
source_conflicts: DeepSeek's `dcgmi diag --memtest` is not the documented current selector; official syntax uses `-r/--run memtest`, matching the source.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly rejects the read-only label, adds workload isolation, DCGM compatibility, ECC/thermal baselines and restoration. It leaves source-versus-DeepSeek syntax unresolved despite official support for `-r memtest`, does not make the source's implicit all-GPU target auditable, and does not explicitly restore each GPU's individual pre-test persistence state.

applicable_history.decision: The historical record treats this as a host-side single run with DCGM, but retains DeepSeek's unsupported command form and supplies no target or state-restoration details.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: V3 preserves the active GPU-memory diagnostic and approval requirement, verifies the source's named-test syntax, requires coverage of every recipe GPU, and replaces the unsafe all-off cleanup with per-GPU restoration to the captured baseline.

available_now: The source identifies the canonical DCGM `memtest` and one-run PASS criterion.
Official current DCGM documentation confirms `dcgmi diag -r memtest`, verbose output, explicit entity selection and default all-entity behavior.
Read-only GPU/client/persistence/ECC/thermal/version inventory can be collected before approval.

Workload blackout and MIG/client disposition, maximum runtime/watchdog, lab thermal/power limits and response owner
Authorization for the active memory diagnostic and persistence-mode changes, plus the original-state restoration and OOB recovery plan
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The GPU/platform owner supplies the entity map, compatible DCGM/driver/configuration and result policy; workload owners authorize quiescence; the lab owner approves resource/thermal limits, persistence changes, supervision and recovery.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect GPU UUID/index/BDF/MIG inventory, current clients/processes, DCGM/driver versions, persistence state, ECC/page-remap/XID/thermal/power and OS/BMC baselines without clearing them
Inspect `dcgmi diag --help`, installed plugin/configuration and package provenance to confirm named memtest support; prepare explicit entity and expected-count arguments offline
prohibited_until_closed: Do not launch memtest, evict clients, alter MIG, enable/disable persistence, reset a GPU or clear ECC/log evidence before authorization and workload isolation
Do not use `--memtest`, omit target accounting, accept SKIP/NOT RUN as PASS, shorten/override pattern coverage without owner approval or unconditionally disable persistence after the run
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: All expected GPU UUIDs map to explicit diagnostic entities; compatible DCGM/driver/plugin/configuration is verified; clients are quiesced by owners; timeout/thermal/stop/recovery limits are signed; each persistence baseline has a restoration action; evidence capture can prove a completed result for every target.

revision_candidate.purpose: Run the supported DCGM `memtest` once on every required NVIDIA GPU and verify per-GPU PASS with no unexplained memory, ECC, XID, thermal, driver or platform error.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: An NVIDIA GPU server whose exact GPU model/UUID population, driver and DCGM diagnostic plugin/configuration are qualified, with host and OOB telemetry available and all in-scope workloads quiesced.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Every NVIDIA GPU in the approved SUT recipe. Use explicit entity selection and expected-count validation when supported; retain a result for each UUID. A subset is not equivalent unless the test owner revises scope.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: GPU UUID/entity map; compatible driver/DCGM/plugin/configuration; workload/MIG disposition; diagnostic authorization; timeout, thermal/power and ECC/XID response limits; original per-GPU persistence states; evidence and recovery plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Capture immutable baselines and target map; verify `dcgmi diag -r memtest` support; after approval, apply only required persistence changes to explicit GPUs; run one verbose/structured named memtest for all approved entities under monitoring; preserve complete output and logs; restore each GPU's recorded persistence state; verify every entity and final host/GPU health.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Expected GPU count/UUIDs match inventory; no unauthorized compute/MIG client remains; DCGM/driver/plugin/configuration is supported; adequate memory/resources and thermal/power headroom exist; persistence baseline, timeout, stop rules, evidence paths and OOB recovery are ready.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Version/package provenance; UUID/entity/BDF/MIG/client map; persistence/ECC/page-remap/XID/thermal baseline; exact command/config/hash; full per-entity verbose or JSON output, timestamps, duration and exit code; synchronized host/BMC logs; post-state and per-GPU persistence restoration proof.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The qualified NVIDIA DCGM documentation/configuration for the installed release plus the exact platform owner's GPU inventory, diagnostic coverage and ECC/XID/thermal/error policy.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Treat memtest as an active resource-consuming diagnostic. Do not run with live workloads, guess entities, alter MIG/ECC, clear counters/logs, ignore skipped entities, reset GPUs automatically or leave persistence different from its per-GPU baseline.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: GPU/platform and workload owners approve the target set, quiescence, active diagnostic and state transitions before launch. The engineer judges warnings/counter deltas and final PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owners resolve qualification, workload isolation and anomalous diagnostic results. Once approved, explicit targeting, execution, monitoring, evidence collection, stop handling and exact state restoration can be automated.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On timeout, unexpected client, thermal/power breach, ECC/XID/driver/DCGM failure or host instability, stop through the supported diagnostic path, preserve state/evidence, restore only recorded persistence settings, avoid automatic reset/rerun and use approved OOB/quarantine escalation if normal control is lost.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Target count/UUID mismatch, unsupported or unavailable memtest, active unauthorized client, insufficient memory/headroom, missing approval/baseline/recovery, timeout, thermal/power violation, ECC/XID/driver/DCGM/host failure, incomplete per-GPU output or failed persistence restoration.

identified_defects: DeepSeek uses an unsupported selector and falsely calls the active memory diagnostic read-only.
The source's no-selector command implicitly covers all GPUs, but V2 allows an approved set without explicitly preventing silent subset coverage.
The source's unconditional disable step can corrupt pre-existing per-GPU persistence state.
reason_for_change: Make all-GPU memory coverage and current documented syntax explicit, and prevent the test cleanup from leaving persistence state different from baseline while retaining workload and thermal safeguards.

new_technical_evidence.title: dcgmi diag — NVIDIA DCGM Documentation
new_technical_evidence.version: latest documentation accessed 2026-10-13; installed DCGM release must be recorded
new_technical_evidence.applicability: NVIDIA DCGM release actually qualified on the SUT
new_technical_evidence.supports: `-r/--run memtest` is the canonical named-test selector; `-v` is verbose; default selection without group/entity is all GPUs/all NVIDIA CPUs; diagnostics can consume substantial resources and require workload coordination.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Runtime support depends on loaded plugins, hardware, libraries, privileges and the installed release.

new_technical_evidence.title: DCGM Diagnostics — Memtest Diagnostic
new_technical_evidence.supports: Memtest exercises GPU memory using multiple data/address/stress patterns whose runtimes vary; it is not a read-only inventory query.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The source does not define enabled patterns or an exact required runtime for this platform.

new_technical_evidence.title: NVIDIA System Management Interface — Persistence Mode
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Linux NVIDIA drivers supporting legacy persistence mode
new_technical_evidence.supports: `nvidia-smi -pm` is an immediate device-modification operation, requires root and affects all GPUs unless `-i` selects one.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The platform owner must define whether legacy persistence mode or the persistence daemon is required.

removed_ambiguities: Resolves source versus DeepSeek command spelling in favor of the documented source form.
Makes every recipe GPU an auditable target and rejects silent subset completion.
Defines cleanup as exact per-GPU baseline restoration rather than global disable.
resolved_blockers: Command syntax is resolved by current official documentation; missing packages, policy and approval remain provisionable readiness conditions, not a permanent automation blocker.
remaining_blockers: No active diagnostic or persistence change until compatibility, complete GPU mapping, workload isolation, approval, limits and recovery are confirmed.
PASS remains blocked if any expected GPU lacks a completed PASS result or if errors/state restoration are unresolved.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 turns V2's unresolved syntax into an official command decision, preserves the source's implicit all-GPU scope with per-UUID evidence, and prevents unconditional cleanup from changing pre-test persistence state.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The isolated validator required one supported DCGM memtest covering every GPU UUID with per-GPU results, error/telemetry context and exact restoration of each persistence baseline.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source enables persistence, runs one verbose DCGM named memtest and then disables persistence, with a PASS-without-errors criterion and a 40-minute estimate.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 adds necessary safety controls but leaves syntax unresolved, does not lock all-GPU coverage and does not require per-GPU restoration to exact baseline.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: No memtest or persistence mutation until workloads are quiesced and approved; account for every UUID, monitor active-resource risk and restore each captured persistence state without resets or evidence clearing.
